reference_sql:
WITH ranked AS (  -- one row per product
  SELECT category_id, unit_cost_eur,
         DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_cost_eur DESC) AS cost_level
  FROM products
)
SELECT DISTINCT category_id, unit_cost_eur AS second_cost
FROM ranked
WHERE cost_level = 2
alternatives:
SELECT p.category_id, MAX(p.unit_cost_eur) AS second_cost
FROM products p
WHERE p.unit_cost_eur < (SELECT MAX(p2.unit_cost_eur) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id)
GROUP BY p.category_id

WITH costs AS (  -- one row per category and different unit cost
  SELECT DISTINCT category_id, unit_cost_eur
  FROM products
)
SELECT c.category_id, c.unit_cost_eur AS second_cost
FROM costs c
WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM costs c2 WHERE c2.category_id = c.category_id AND c2.unit_cost_eur > c.unit_cost_eur) = 1

other_way.sql:
SELECT p.category_id, MAX(p.unit_cost_eur) AS second_cost
FROM products p
WHERE p.unit_cost_eur < (SELECT MAX(p2.unit_cost_eur) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id)
GROUP BY p.category_id
other_way.tradeoff: The highest cost below the category's top cost is the classic answer without windows, but it does not stretch to the third or fourth cost.

solver.query:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT category_id, unit_cost_eur,
         DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_cost_eur DESC) AS lvl
  FROM products
  WHERE unit_cost_eur IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT category_id, unit_cost_eur AS second_cost
FROM d
WHERE lvl = 2
GROUP BY category_id, unit_cost_eur
